messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired: inference-queue-backlog-high on cluster-prod (severity: P1). queue_length=8420, saturation=98%, autoscaler_lag=3m

pagerduty: PagerDuty INC-2026-4711 triggered (unacked). routed to oncall:emma.

emma: acked. i'm looking. first pass: is this autoscaler failing to react or nodes provisioning slow?

raj: seeing a lot of pods in Pending with reason=Insufficient resources and NodeProvisionTimeout in the cloud provider logs. autoscaler has 12 pending scale attempts in the last 2m.

matt: confirmed high token backlog in the inference queue (apiserver log snippet):
```
2026-03-15T02:11:12Z backlog_size=8420 target_latency_ms=200 actual_latency_ms=1720
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z enqueue_rate=1200/s process_rate=150/s
```

emma: ok. impact = customer facing latency spikes and a subset of requests 429'ing due to queue taildrop. cc @sophia for manual scaling.

sophia: joining. i'm on GCP console now. nodes are stuck in PROVISIONING state; quota looks fine but there are repeated attach/detach failures for the gpu-lvm disk class.

raj: autoscaler logs show backoff: "scale_attempt_failed: provider_attach_error; next_attempt_in=45s". The controller treats attaches as terminal until backoff resets; that explains autoscaler lag.

emma: mitigation plan: 1) divert burst traffic to fallback-region (eu-west fallback) 2) manually spin up a smaller non-GPU pool with ephemeral quantized model to drain the hot queue 3) temporary increase queue retention to avoid taildrop. I'll run commands.

matt: +1. suggest also disabling new long-running batch jobs to free capacity.

emma: running manual scaling (kubectl):
```bash
kubectl scale deployment inference-ephemeral --replicas=40 -n prod
# verify pods
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-ephemeral
```

incident-bot: Action: manual-scale executed by emma. deployment/inference-ephemeral scaled to 40 replicas.

raj: started gcloud instance create for preemptible non-gpu pool to take CPU-bound traffic. command logged. provisioning events now show nodes become Ready but kubelet has ImagePullBackOff on one image — retrying.

sophia: workaround applied: switched PVC storageClass from gpu-lvm to standard-ssd for the ephemeral pool. new nodes booting cleanly.

matt: traffic diversion: routed 15% of inference traffic to eu-west via smart-routing policy to reduce immediate pressure.

emma: stats update: backlog down from 8420 -> 2400 in 7m after scaling and diversion. taildrop errors reduced from 14% -> 1.2%. still above normal but improving.

pagerduty: INC-2026-4711 acknowledged by emma at 1783456820. escalation to SRE sent to oncall group.

raj: noticed autoscaler controller still logging provider_attach_error for GPU pool. we should mark that pool unhealthy and avoid routing new requests there until further investigation.

emma: marking gpu-pool-prod as degraded in console (routing policy updated). setting fallback to cpu-quant models for new sessions.

matt: customers note draft: "We've detected elevated inference latencies and intermittent request failures yesterday. We've mitigated by diverting some traffic and adding temporary capacity; teams are investigating root cause and will follow up with a postmortem." Anyone want to edit?

sophia: add ETA for next update in 30m and call out that low-latency regions restored for most customers.

emma: will send customer update in 15m. assigning follow-ups: raj to dig into provider attach failures, sophia to own short-term routing and storage workaround, matt to collect metrics for postmortem, me (emma) owning overall incident and postmortem writeup.

raj: quick finding: cloud provider is returning intermittent "volume attach timeout" for the gpu-lvm disks tied to a particular hypervisor pool. filing support ticket, will request force-migration for affected volumes.

matt: can we patch controller to reduce backoff aggression in the short term? there is a flag --scale-backoff-ms. we could lower it from 30000 -> 5000 to allow quicker retry attempts while support works on the attach issue. risk is thundering; we'll keep manual gating.

emma: ok to patch to 5s for short window. patching now to canary cell and watching.

incident-bot: Deploy event: autoscaler-controller patch applied by emma to canary cells. flag --scale-backoff-ms=5000.

emma: canary looks good, no thrash. autoscaler attempts increased and some attach attempts succeeded; new nodes for gpu pool still flaky but ephemeral CPU pool handling load.

matt: backlog down to 600 in last 12m. metrics: request latency median back to ~260ms for routed traffic, but gpu-heavy jobs still have elevated tails.

pagerduty: INC-2026-4711 status: acknowledged -> monitoring.

emma: handing off to night oncall (raj) at 1783457200. next steps in handoff: continue gpu attach investigation, keep routing policy in fallback mode until confirmed stable, prepare postmortem template. I've posted the mitigation runbook in #eng-oncall.

raj: ack. I'll keep pager duty rotation warm and update in 30m or on new developments.

matt: logging final note before handoff: root cause hypothesis = intermittent block device attach failures on gpu-lvm storage in a hypervisor cohort causing autoscaler to backoff; mitigation = route traffic, manual ephemeral pool spin-up, temporary backoff reduction; impact = elevated latency and some 429s for ~25 minutes during peak. Postmortem assigned to emma with helpers raj/matt/sophia.

incident-bot: Incident update (INC-2026-4711): mitigations in place, oncall handoff completed, monitoring.

emma: :white_check_mark: closing timeline here. will start postmortem doc in the morning and link to this thread. thanks team.
